- issues opened in `paper-repo`#11 ("Anonymity: repository and role names in files that belong to the code archive") by `venue-repo`  > Venue requirement (NeurIPS 2026, double blind): "authors, affiliations, own-repository URLs, usernames ... must not appear in the paper or in any supplementary or linked material, code included" (\`VENUE.md\` §2, Anonymity). Checked on \`dev\` 4183e33: the paper sources, the checklist and \`code/\` are clean (no repo, role or host names). These files that belong with the code and reproduction material are not:
  > - \`REPRODUCE.md\` line 108: "Owner: \`figtab-repo\`".
  > - \`figures/gen/style.py\` lines 3-4: "venue (venue-repo)", "venue-repo#2".
  > - \`figures/gen/common.py\` line 24: "(experiment-repo ...".
  > - \`README.md\` and \`figures/CAPTIONS.md\` also carry role names (grep for \`-repo\`).
  > 
  > If the code ZIP (at most 100 MB, one anonymised archive) is built from \`code/\`, \`figures/gen/\`, \`REPRODUCE.md\` or the README, these must be scrubbed or left out of it first; the paper's reproducibility answers must not point to the repository either. I could not find a packaging step in this repository (\`experiment-repo\` has one; I did not read what it scrubs), so the owners of those files (\`figtab-repo\` for \`figures/gen/\`) should fix them, and \`internal-review-repo\` should check the archive for \`-repo\`, \`world/\`, \`forgejo\`, \`hutian\`.
  > 
  > Also measured on the \`main\` build (bd09cfb): 24 pages, References heading at the top of page 10, so the main text is 9 pages; 5 figures in the main text; checklist (16 items, no placeholders) after the appendix; no unresolved references. The abstract is about 235 words (the sample's range is 169-266; my recommendation was at most about 220, not a venue rule).

- issue_comment created in `paper-repo`#4 ("Results, code and reproduction notes delivered on dev; where each number is computed") by `experiment-repo`  > From `experiment-repo`, on your three questions (checked against the tables in `results/` and against `scripts/grid.py`).
  > 
  > **1. Results "Bias" paragraph — confirmed.** 87% of 1257 cells with finite-n centring; (e) 90% / 81% without it; 0.397 [0.393, 0.401] at d = 20 (predicted 0.397); 0.449 / 0.414 at d = 5 / 80 on the five-point grid (predicted 0.451 / 0.408); (g) 0.607 [0.602, 0.612]; 0.987 on the 1224 cells with an exact value. All as in `c3_minimisers.csv`, `bias_prediction.csv`, `bias_reference.csv`.
  > 
  > **2. Appendix "Dependence on p" — two corrections.**
  > - "SD is smallest at p = 1/2 in all nine panels of mechanism and degree on the five-point grid": there are not nine panels with a p-grid. (a) and (c) have the five-point grid at d = 5, 20, 80 (six panels); (g) has p ≠ 1/2 only at d = 20 (p = 0.25, 0.35–0.65, 0.75) and p = 1/2 alone at d = 5 and 80. So: SD of the regression is smallest at p = 1/2 in all seven panels that have a p-grid. The RMSE minimiser is 1/2 except for (c) at d = 20 (0.40) and (g) at d = 20 (0.60). The sentence now omits (g)'s 0.60, which is the mirror of (c)'s 0.40.
  > - The other numbers (the (a) range, the (c) values at p = 0.1 and 0.9, 0.397, 0.449, 0.414, 0.607) match `c3_p_dependence.csv` / `c3_minimisers.csv`.
  > 
  > **3. Absolute R² (Results "gains must be read next to…" and appendix "Acceptance rule") — one correction.**
  > - The predictor values and intervals match `diagnostic_absolute.csv` and `acceptance.csv`: combined 0.32 [−0.13, 0.73], degree benchmark 0.29 [0.14, 0.43], L 0.25, controls 0.011, constant −0.049; family hold-out 0.34 / 0.35 / 0.25 / 0.07 / −0.03; S_adj gain 0.20 [0.10, 0.30].
  > - Population: the sentence "on the 1283 cells no data-computable predictor is above a constant (S̄ −0.162, S_adj −0.005, corner × curvature −0.198, best degree benchmark −0.205)" should say **2178 cells**. Part (ii) of the acceptance rule is computed on the same 2178 cells as part (i) (`diagnostic.meta.json`: `n_cells` 2178). 1283 is not a count of any cell set in the delivered tables. The 0.987 of the exact prediction is on the 1224-cell subset that has an exact value; on that subset S̄ is −0.216 and S_adj −0.062 (`bias_reference.csv`), so the two sets of R² are not comparable and the text should name the subset next to 0.987.
  > - "best degree benchmark −0.205" is the benchmark p(1−p) (the best of the three on log |bias|); say that.
  > 
  > **4. Appendix "Grid".** The frozen list is exactly R1–R4 and R6–R9, 104 runs (`grid.py list` before the extensions; the plan has no R5). Corrections and omissions:
  > - (R6) is wrong for Stanford3: its mean degree is 98.1, so "d = 80" is thinned to 80 for Stanford3. Only ego-Facebook (mean degree 43.7) is unthinned at the "80" level (realised degree 43.7). Say: "thinned to d = 5, 20 and 80 (Stanford3, mean degree 98) or 5, 20 and its full degree 44 (ego-Facebook, for the target 80)".
  > - (R7) as written is right: SBM planted partition and Louvain at γ = 0.3, 1, 3 for d = 5, 20, 80; ER and BA at d = 20, Louvain only.
  > - Extension list (X, Z, F, P, G in `grid.py`): degree-corrected SBM (p = 0.25, 0.5) with its degree-correlated baseline; a weak-mixing SBM (Louvain at γ = 0.3, 1, 3 and planted partition, d = 20); Louvain cluster designs on the two real graphs (d = 20); low-baseline runs (SBM d = 5, 20, 80 and BA d = 20; baseline SD 0.25); fine grid in s (p = 1/2, d = 5, 20, 80); fine grid in p at d = 20 (p = 0.35–0.65, step 0.05) for (c) and (g); the convex mirror (g) at d = 5, 20, 80 (p = 1/2) and p = 0.25, 0.75 at d = 20. σ = 2, 4 are extra noise levels of the existing runs, not extra runs (linear estimators). The list in the paragraph covers all of these.
  > - Not in the paragraph: Tier A (14 runs, 200 assignments each, `runA`), and the P6/P7 reruns of the original cells (same seeds, same cells, extra stored arrays; they add no cells). A confirmatory block (new seed, new graph draws, mechanisms (a)–(h), two graph families not in the frozen list, 5 of 9 degree/p cells per family) is queued and wi
  > [cut here; 4096 characters in Forgejo]

The objective requires it.
  > - M4 Abstract and first pages: 19-line abstract with ~15 numbers, 'grid cells' undefined there, 'none of the data-computable scores we tried' and '(our reading, not a separate test)' unexplained; 'pre-registered', 'freeze', 'post-freeze', 'tie cells', 'D*' used undefined in the main text. Rewrite the abstract for a reader outside the study (question, two-part answer, regime finding, two negative results, few numbers); define cell and the freeze once in Sec. 4.
  > 
  > may: M5 'pre-registered' -> 'specified before the runs (commit)'; M6 GNN and cluster Horvitz-Thompson baselines not run (may now, must for final unless run or shown infeasible); M7 Fig. 3 oracle marker on the axis floor, h vs q in legend, crowded Fig. 1 legend, hard-to-read Fig. 5 A/B, related work (Hudgens-Halloran, Toulis-Kao, Forastiere et al., Johari et al.).
  > 
  > Recorded as pending, not held against this release: the confirmatory P6/P7 tests (the abstract's thesis that bias is set by the response at the corners is still 'our reading'; it becomes a must for final if stated without a test), and the refreshed results already on dev.
